problem: Let $I=[0,2]⊂R$ and ${X}_{i}={i}\times [0,i].$ Which of the following represents ${⋂}_{i\in I}{X}_{i}?$

examples.knowledge_point: Visualizing Intersections of Uncountable Families of Indexed Sets
examples.problem: Let $I = [0,1] \subset \mathbb{R}$ and $X_i = [-i, 0] \times [-1,1].$ Sketch a representation of $\displaystyle \bigcap_{i \in I} X_i$ in the Cartesian plane.
examples.worked_solution:
Recall that the intersection of a family of indexed sets consists of those elements that belong to *all* the sets:

$$
\bigcap_{i \in I} A_i = \big\{ x \: : \: x \in A_k \:\:\textrm{for all}\:\: k \in I \big\}
$$

Let's now write down one of our indexed sets. For example, if $i=0.5,$ we have 

$$
X_{0.5} = [-0.5,0] \times [-1, 1] = \big\{ (a,b) \: : \: a \in [-0.5, 0], b \in [-1, 1] \big\}.
$$

This represents a rectangle whose vertices are at $(-0.5, -1),$ $(-0.5, 1),$ $(0, 1),$ and $(0, -1)$ in the coordinate plane, as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14072804/assets/8ad650cb3f2fa4da920a442e8cc1b24af5027595cba4e43138eff2126cf4c102.png)

In general,

$$
X_i = [-i, 0] \times [-1,1] = \big\{ (a,b) \: : \: a \in [-i, 0], b \in [-1, 1] \big\}
$$

is the rectangle whose vertices are at $(-i,-1),$ $(-i,1),$ $(0, 1),$ and $(0, -1).$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14072804/assets/a37cfa508cf3a60536084fbc1e57c5aeac3414904d2ad72ef1deda85dc4eddd8.png)

 

The intersection of all these rectangles is the line segment $\{0\}\times [-1,1]{:}$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14072804/assets/5e9a611629f4370c57e77a057439c759670afa17c14c4b2339e1d471f616ea72.png)

feedback.problem: Let $I=[-1,1]⊂R$ and ${X}_{i}={i}\times [-|i|,|i|].$ Which of the following represents ${⋃}_{i\in I}{X}_{i}?$
feedback.worked_solution:
Recall that the union of a family of indexed sets consists of those elements that belong to *at least one* set:

$$
{⋃}_{i\in I}{A}_{i}={x\,:\,x\in {A}_{k}\,\,\text{for at least one}\,\,k\in I}
$$

Let's now write down one of our indexed sets. For example, if $i=-0.5,$ we have 

$$
{X}_{-0.5}={-0.5}\times [-0.5,0.5]={(-0.5,k)\,:\,k\in [-0.5,0.5]}.
$$

This represents a vertical line segment from the point $(-0.5,-0.5)$ to the point $(-0.5,0.5)$ in the coordinate plane, as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14072804/assets/b7793d85e02ccd05c55c34971c90be087d58274eabd21f46fe09f08ccd60797b.png)

In general,

$$
{X}_{i}={i}\times [-|i|,|i|]={(i,k)\,:\,k\in [-|i|,|i|]}
$$

is the vertical line segment from the point $(i,-|i|)$ to the point $(i,|i|).$ 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14072804/assets/c30712295adfe51c655662cc09f8f1e23b3ea97573693154e0e0b6ba48e15c07.png)

As $i$ runs over $I,$ these line segments sweep the following figure that represents the union ${⋃}_{i\in I}{X}_{i}:$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14072804/assets/8ce0c60aafe1a41b372c1f1477241c584d6f8ae224113c360576feb37fc25a8c.png)
